title: Subgroups Matter for Robust Bias Mitigation
benchmark_measurement: The impact of using different religious subgroup definitions (e.g., any mention of religion vs. mention of Christianity) on the performance of bias mitigation techniques in a toxicity classification task.
findings: For the toxicity prediction task on the Civil_comments dataset, using religious affiliation as the subgroup for bias mitigation was generally less effective and sometimes detrimental compared to using subgroups based on the actual spurious correlate (mention of gender). The study also found no significant difference in performance when using coarse (any mention of religion) versus granular (mention of Christianity) religious subgroups for mitigation, suggesting that increasing granularity for the 'wrong' attribute does not improve results.
